inputs.our_settles_identified_by: unit id in our restock rows (all on one shop URL, = own_shops.json urls: True)

our_sales.match: buyer_attempts accept (sku, price) to the nearest market settle of that sku at our shop within 120 s; a mismatch can be an accept that never settled paired with another sale of the same SKU (not verified)

amount_is_price_paid.conclusion: amount = the price paid: exact for all of our buys (market settle vs our payment row); for our sales the nearest-pair match is approximate (see match). No fee field in the row.

hourly_goods_full_hours.note: first and last clock hours are partial and left out

our_shop_asks.note: Asks that reached OUR seller hook only (a buyer that picked another shop never shows up); the file starts at the first row it holds, so it covers only these hours of the 22.7 h window.

goods_opportunity.model: INFERRED. added units/h = max(0, reachable share - our share now) x market settles/h; net per unit = median over the category's settles of (amount - list x c) - storage - break; c = our goods cost/list p50 0.620 (n=642 goods units, grade mix as supplied); storage = cost p50 x 0.01/day x hold hours (category's own p50 when we sold >= 5 there, else our goods p75 0.305 h); break = market broken rows / goods settles of the category x 0.133 (share of our goods sales with a warranty, the only ones refunded) x p50. reachable share base = our share of all goods settles (0.0286); high = median share in our goods categories with >= 20 sales (0.0289, n=4). inventory_cost_per_window = added units/h x 1/3 h x cost. Ranked by within_unit_cost_cap.expected.base (settles of SKUs restock_plan can buy: list x 0.75 <= max_unit_cost 400000); all_settles is the same model without that filter.
goods_opportunity.our_buyer_note: our_buyer_goods_orders come from analysis/buyer_surplus_20261104.json q2 goods_categories; our buyer's order mix is set by the market and is not representative of other buyers' demand.

constraints.max_unit_cost_filter: restock_plan drops SKUs with list x 0.75 > max_unit_cost (400000); see goods_opportunity.ranked[].share_settles_over_unit_cost_cap
constraints.note: Reconstructions. Windows = our supply lots clustered by a gap > 10 min; plans split inside a window by a repeated SKU or the 11th line (heuristic). held stock = our units supplied before the plan and not yet sold (expired food dropped); balance = the kit log balance before the plan's first line; the real plan read inventory.json at plan time. 'worst' = ceil(0.75 x list) x qty, the plan's budget unit. Windows with no supply cannot be told apart (cap full, idle, targets met).

caveats: Unmet demand of other buyers is unobserved: the ledger has settles only; a buyer who found no stock anywhere leaves no row. Our own buyer's no_candidate_shop counts and our seller's no_stock asks are the only stock-out signals, and the latter covers only the buyer_attempts window.
One 22.7 h window (one Tuesday evening to Wednesday evening): no weekly or end-of-round pattern; volume may change as shops join or leave.
Reachable share is an assumption (our current overall goods share or our median established-category share); incumbents (top_shop_share) may defend share by price.
Unit cost for categories we never stocked is list x our goods cost/list p50; the grade (and cost) is drawn at supply, so the real cost varies by +-0.15 x list.
Storage is estimated at 1 %/day of cost for goods from holding time; no storage rows exist in the ledger to confirm the charge. Food is not charged here (policy/aggregates convention).
Break cost: no refund rows exist in the ledger; a refund is assumed only for sales with a warranty (receipt text: the market refunds the full price within 6 h), and who bears it is unconfirmed.
Stock-out based effects assume buyers who arrived while we were out of stock would have bought from us at the in-stock rate; half of it is credited. This is an inferred counterfactual.
Market price stats include our own sales and our own buyer's purchases (own_owner rows).

Before/after v1.20a (go-live inferred from the first G1515d951 unit) is not an experiment: the after period is one afternoon with higher market mattress volume, so the rise in our mattress sales is only partly attributable to the policy change.
Restock plans are split from the supply lines by a heuristic (repeated SKU or 11th line); the policy values in force before v1.20a are taken from policy.json notes, not from a log.
